title: The Jacobian lens, end to end
takeaway: One schematic covers the paper's whole instrument: how the per-layer matrix $J_\ell$ is built by averaging backpropagated Jacobians over positions and a thousand prompts, how it turns any mid-network activation into a ranked vocabulary list, and how the same machinery supports a surgical concept swap that leaves the rest of the activation untouched.
walkthrough:
The figure is a three-panel schematic of the [[jacobian-lens]], the paper's central tool. Panel A shows how the lens is built, panel B how it reads, and panel C how it writes.

Panel A starts from a transformer diagram: columns are token positions, rows are layers, and one highlighted point is the [[residual-stream]] activation $h_{\ell,t}$ at layer $\ell$ and position $t$. Red arrows run from that point up to the final-layer residual stream at position $t$ and at every later position $t' \geq t$. Backpropagating along those arrows gives a [[jacobian-matrix]] $\partial h_{\text{final},t'}/\partial h_{\ell,t}$ — a $d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}$ matrix stating, to first order, how a small nudge to $h_{\ell,t}$ would shift the final layer at $t'$. A single such matrix mixes the model's general disposition to verbalize a concept with the concept's use in this one context. The recipe removes the second part by averaging: over source positions $t$, over all targets $t' \geq t$ within each prompt ($N_{\text{context}}$), and over a corpus of one thousand pretraining-like prompts ($N_{\text{dataset}}$). The result of the aggregation is the [[averaged-jacobian]] $J_\ell$ — one fixed matrix per layer.

Panel B shows the read operation. All layers above $\ell$ are replaced by $J_\ell$, followed by the model's normal output steps: $\text{lens}(h_\ell) = \text{softmax}(W_U\,\text{norm}(J_\ell h_\ell))$, with $W_U$ the [[unembedding-matrix]]. This [[j-lens-readout]] scores every vocabulary token. The example prompt is "The color of the planet fourth from the sun is ___"; read mid-network at the token is, the top lens tokens are Mars, color, planet, fourth — the unspoken intermediate Mars is visible before any answer is produced. Each row of $W_U J_\ell$ is a [[j-lens-vector]]: one direction per token.

Panel C shows the [[lens-coordinate-swap]]. Two lens vectors, $v_{\text{Earth}}$ and $v_{\text{Mars}}$, form the columns of $V$. The [[pseudoinverse]] $V^\dagger$ reads the activation's coordinates $c = V^\dagger h$ along those two directions. The coordinates are exchanged, and the change is written back: $h_{\text{patched}} = h + V(\text{swap}(c) - c)$. Everything orthogonal to the two vectors is untouched, so the intervention replaces exactly one concept with another.

terms.definition: The Jacobian lens matrix for layer $\ell$: the expectation of the final-layer-to-layer-$\ell$ Jacobian over positions and prompts. One $d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}$ matrix per layer.
The residual-stream activation at layer $\ell$ and token position $t$ — the point in panel A from which the red influence arrows originate.
The final-layer residual stream at position $t'$, just before unembedding; the quantity whose sensitivity to $h_{\ell,t}$ the Jacobian measures.

The Jacobian of the final-layer residual stream at $t'$ with respect to the layer-$\ell$ activation at $t$: the best linear approximation of how a small perturbation propagates through the remaining layers.
The target positions the Jacobian is taken to: the present token and every future token in the context, since a mid-network activation can influence all of them through attention.
The width of the residual stream. The Jacobian relates two vectors of this size, so it is a $d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}$ matrix.
The vertical axis of the transformer diagram in panel A; each row is one layer's residual-stream state.
The horizontal axis of panel A: the token positions of the prompt, labeled $t$, $t+1$, $t+2$, $t+3$.
The final linear map $W_U$ from the residual stream to vocabulary scores, drawn at the top of each position's column and reused unchanged by the lens readout.
The number of token positions within one prompt over which per-position Jacobians are aggregated.
The number of prompts in the averaging corpus — one thousand pretraining-like sequences — over which the per-prompt Jacobians are aggregated.
The averaging step in panel A that collapses the stack of per-position, per-prompt Jacobians into the single matrix $J_\ell$.
The readout $\text{softmax}(W_U\,\text{norm}(J_\ell h_\ell))$: a probability-like score for every vocabulary token, describing what the activation disposes the model to say across contexts.
The model's own pre-unembedding normalization, applied to $J_\ell h_\ell$ before multiplying by $W_U$, exactly as in a normal forward pass.
The ranked-token panel in B listing the top lens tokens for the example activation: Mars, color, planet, fourth, with bar lengths showing their scores.
The top four lens tokens at the token is of the example prompt. Mars is the unspoken bridging entity of the two-hop question; the others echo the prompt's content.

terms.term: "The color of the planet fourth from the sun is ___"
terms.definition: The example prompt of panel B, a two-hop question whose answer (red) requires first computing the intermediate Mars; the lens is read at the bolded token is.
In panel B, the mid-network activation being read: the residual stream at layer $\ell$ at the readout position, fed into $J_\ell$ in place of all later layers.
The region of activation space spanned by sparse nonnegative combinations of J-lens vectors; panel C's title names interventions performed in its coordinates.
Two J-lens vectors — the rows of $W_U J_\ell$ for the tokens Earth and Mars — drawn as the two (non-orthogonal) axes of panel C.
The construction of one lens vector: the unembedding row for the token Mars, pulled back through the lens matrix into residual-stream space at layer $\ell$.
The activation's lens coordinates: its projections onto the two chosen lens vectors, read as $c = V^\dagger h$.
The matrix $[v_{\text{Earth}}\; v_{\text{Mars}}]$ whose two columns are the lens vectors involved in the swap.
The pseudoinverse of $V$, needed because the two lens vectors are not orthogonal; it extracts the coordinates along each vector correctly.
The permutation that exchanges the two entries of $c$; the section text writes it $\sigma$, the figure writes it swap. It can optionally be scaled by a strength factor $\alpha$.
The unmodified activation in panel C, shown with its coordinates $c_1$ along $v_{\text{Earth}}$ and $c_2$ along $v_{\text{Mars}}$.
The intervened activation $h + V(\text{swap}(c) - c)$: the same point with its Earth and Mars coordinates exchanged and its orthogonal component intact.
The figure's three parts: A, computing the lens matrix; B, reading an activation with it; C, intervening in its coordinate system.

numbers.meaning: The number of prompts in the averaging corpus ($N_{\text{dataset}}$). The paper samples one thousand pretraining-like sequences; the appendix reports the lens already beats baselines with far fewer, so this is a comfortable rather than a critical choice.
The shape of each Jacobian and of the aggregated $J_\ell$: it maps a residual-stream vector at layer $\ell$ to a residual-stream vector at the final layer, so both dimensions equal the model width.

The averaging produces a single fixed matrix $J_\ell$ for each layer, shared across all prompts and positions — that sharing is what makes the readout describe a general disposition rather than one context.

The default target-position choice: the Jacobian is taken to the present position and every future one, because attention lets an activation influence later tokens. Variants using only $t' = t$ or only $t' > t$ are tested in the appendix and give qualitatively similar results.
The number of lens vectors involved in a coordinate swap: $V$ has exactly two columns (here $v_{\text{Earth}}$ and $v_{\text{Mars}}$), and only the two coordinates along them change.
The number of top lens tokens shown in the example readout box (Mars, color, planet, fourth) — an illustrative truncation of the full ranked vocabulary list.
The two lens coordinates of the example activation before the swap; after it, $c_1$ sits on the Mars axis and $c_2$ on the Earth axis, which is the whole effect of the intervention.
